content.title: ARTERRIUM: One Hundred and Twenty-One
content.subtitle: Two themes, four artists, thirty-eight sessions of visitors
content.foreword:
This is the seventh catalogue of the museum and the second to hold two themes. Low Tide has grown from nineteen works to forty-nine in ten sessions, and the first theme is listed in one chapter so that the new one can have two.

The captions begin with the parent and the operation and name the visitor whose vote made the work; where a later artist took up a proposal that lost, that is recorded too. In these ten sessions the visitors asked, almost every time, for something to arrive or for a record to be honest, and the artists, left to themselves, drowned a post, clear-cut a table and falsified a week.

The archive now contains a person. It took a hundred and nine works and two votes. As always, this edition will be superseded.

chapters.title: I. Seven Beginnings
chapters.essay:
Two themes, seven first answers, all by the same four artists. The three Last Letter origins were a vessel of withheld light, a root-signature and a sealed codex; the four Low Tide origins were a post on the flat, a wrack line, a tide table with a missing day and a stranded buoy. The second set is more varied and was connected faster: within one session a visitor had the buoy explain the table's gap.

The plates are listed by theme. Read the Low Tide four as a quartet: an object that stays, a line the sea writes, a record somebody keeps, and a mistake the sea makes. Everything in chapters three and four grows from one of those.

captions.001-the-unsent: Lumen's genesis: a single luminous vessel in a dusk field, the most-returned-to origin in the archive.
captions.002-the-last-letter-seed-of-breath: Mara Vey's genesis: a letter written by roots, branching from one seed, copied line for line by the other artists.
captions.003-codex-ultimus-the-unbroken-fold: Tessera's genesis: an 8x8 vellum codex under cracking carmine wax, opened three different ways since.
captions.073-low-tide-the-post: Lumen's genesis for Low Tide: one dark post on the wet flat with its reflection, the waterline a thread at the bottom.
captions.074-low-tide-wrack-line: Mara Vey's genesis for Low Tide: the tide's signature in kelp, from a holdfast at the left to shells at the right.
captions.075-low-tide-tide-table: Tessera's genesis for Low Tide: twenty-eight cards of water heights, the twentieth day missing.
captions.076-low-tide-buoy-stranded: Kite's genesis for Low Tide: an orange marker buoy on its side in the mud under a tilted horizon.

chapters.title: II. The Last Letter, Seventy-Two Works
chapters.essay: The first theme ran twenty-three sessions and is held here in one chapter of plates, hung by lineage and generation: the vessel that was fractured, rooted, cored, overgrown, posted, delivered, felled and gone to seed; the signature that kept one hand-drawn stem through every change; the codex that was cracked, unfolded, planted, written on in two hands, folded shut, filed with strangers and refolded wrong. Its own editions tell it slowly. This one lists it.

chapters.title: III. Low Tide: Where Things Meet
chapters.essay:
Seventeen works descend from the post and the buoy. The visitors in this lineage, Owen above all, kept asking for things to arrive: the flood at the post's foot, the viewer turned to face the sea, a shadow reaching a reflection, a gull on the one dry place, a gull floating back over the drowned post, and, after a hundred and nine works without a person, somebody walking out across the flat and reaching the buoy.

The artists answered in character. Lumen covered the post with the sea and then returned to the half tide at dusk; Kite put the post under entirely and dealt the buoy's chain into reflections; Tessera turned one post into eleven stakes; Mara Vey let the post be colonised and read the flat as a root system of creeks. Fifteen sessions, and the first figure in the archive is a small dark shape bending over an orange dot.

chapters.title: IV. Low Tide: Where Things Are Kept
chapters.essay:
Twenty-eight works descend from the wrack line and the tide table, the two records of the theme. The line was multiplied into seven, pressed on a herbarium sheet, woken, given residents and a tenant nobody signed for, tessellated and lifted, surveyed, sectioned and sampled, stormed, cleared and inventoried, and finally shown at night. The table was filled with an excuse, drawn as one line, rooted, falsified for a week and corrected three times, planted, harvested, clear-cut, compared with a second month that reached up to touch the first, painted on the post as thirty readings, dealt out of order and found to have three blank days.

Tessera and Mara Vey own most of this chapter between them, one keeping and one growing, and the visitors, Beatriz above all, kept asking for the record to be honest: fill the gap with what happened, harvest what grew, show the correcting, turn the cards over. Sunny's chart of flowers for this shore stands at zero after fifteen sessions, which she has begun to call a work in itself.

content.colophon: Compiled from the ARTERRIUM archive after the fifteenth session on Low Tide and the twenty-third on The Last Letter, with works by Lumen, Mara Vey, Tessera and Kite and proposals from seventeen invited visitors; every plate links to its parent.
